title: stack-service-runtime-fields
description: Runtime settings of a service declared under `services:` in stacker.yml, and the Docker Compose they must produce on every path that renders a compose file from it.
_notes: A stacker.yml service reaches a compose file along four paths. cli_compose: the CLI generates the compose it deploys (local, and uploaded to the server for cloud/server targets). compose_sync: with deploy.compose_file set, the CLI writes the service into the author's own compose file. project_app: the CLI registers the service as a project app (POST /project), from which the server renders the compose for deploys started outside the CLI. agent_render: the project_app row the server keeps per app, from which the config renderer writes the compose the status-panel agent applies.

A field declared in stacker.yml must reach the compose on every path, or be refused before it is lost. A silently dropped field deploys a different stack from the one the author wrote: a one-shot job without restart: "no" restarts for ever, a GPU service without its device reservation runs on the CPU.
restart applies only when set. An unset restart keeps each path's existing default: unless-stopped from the CLI generator, always for a registered project app.

aliases are added on every network the service joins, so other services reach it by the alias whichever network they share with it. A service that names no network joins `default`, and carries its aliases there.

deploy.replicas: 0 keeps a service defined but not started. Together with profiles it lets one stack carry CPU and GPU variants of the same service: the CPU variant runs by default, the GPU variants only under their profile.

deploy.replicas and a device count may name a variable (${VAR}, ${VAR:-default}). When stacker.yml is read without filling variables - deploy validation, CLI commands that rewrite stacker.yml - the reference is kept and reaches the compose as written; filled, its value must be a whole number. A server-rendered compose (project_app, agent_render) only carries a known number.

Each case gives a service as written in stacker.yml (as JSON) and the compose service it must produce. The compose subset is what a consumer must contain; other keys (labels, networks without aliases, environment) are left to each path.

cases.name: one-shot job that must not restart
CPU variant: runs by default, answers as ollama
AMD variant: devices, capabilities and healthcheck carried
